tools.name: bf_catalogue
tools.description: Lists every Business Frameworks node: handle, title, layer, token count, price, whether it is free, and whether its decision rule can be run on numbers. Business Frameworks is operating judgement for running a business from launch to about $50M in revenue: one equation, the terms and branches under

tools.name: bf_read_node
tools.description: Returns one node with its citations and a cite-as line; `variant` is full (default), terse (the lede alone) or agent (the text as fields: scope, inputs, rule, action, check, units, example, apply, recheck, recheck_note, closing_citation), one price. Free nodes (marked in bf_catalogue) cost nothing;

tools.name: bf_decision_schema
tools.description: Returns the input schema, an example input, the price and the fit record (what the framework does for this decision by model, before paying) for one of the applied decisions (reinvest or distribute, build or run for cash, cash cycle, runway, owner pay, hurdle rate, concentration, pace of growth, pri

tools.name: bf_apply_decision
tools.description: Runs one decision node's rule on the numbers you send and returns the computed figures, a verdict, the actions in order, the check to keep and the node text with its citations. Deterministic: the result comes from the published rule, not from a model. Costs the decision's catalogue price ($0.05, USD

tools.name: bf_resolve
tools.description: Quotes the minimal set of nodes that answers a broad task — a decision bundle, a market (chain) bundle or a cross bundle — with its price — one flat price, USD 0.05, with or without its scale band — stated before anything is paid. Deterministic and free: a named bundle or decision wins, then the inp

tools.name: bf_read_bundle
tools.description: Returns the nodes of one bundle in order — the central node full, the supporting nodes terse — with citations and a cite-as line per node, on one settlement at the quoted price (a flat $0.05 for every bundle, band included; USDC on Base over x402). Pass the bundle id from bf_resolve or bf_catalogue,

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: bf_read_bundle · Private data: bf_catalogue, bf_decision_schema · Public sink: bf_apply_decision · Destructive: bf_catalogue, bf_decision_schema.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: bf_read_bundle · Private data: bf_catalogue, bf_decision_schema · Public sink: bf_apply_decision · Destructive: bf_catalogue, bf_decision_schema

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
